From 0a3bd5018ad72b6e9e4ea86755f8e4ecdc755ba0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: magnum <john.magnum@hushmail.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Dec 2017 11:47:21 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Bug fix for SAP-G format, problem introduced in 27c9bf17.
 SIMD_COEF_32 was tested before defined. Also down-tunes OMP_SCALE so it
 resembles the multiplier used for length sorting. Closes #3050.


diff --git a/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c b/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
index f7e897106..77d0c87d2 100644
--- a/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
+++ b/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
@@ -25,15 +25,6 @@ john_register_one(&fmt_sapG);
 
 #if defined(_OPENMP)
 #include <omp.h>
-#ifndef OMP_SCALE
-#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
-// Some OMP scaling moved into max_keys, so that we can have more values in SIMD
-// mode, to sort hashes by limb size.  (TODO)
-#define OMP_SCALE               128
-#else
-#define OMP_SCALE               2048
-#endif
-#endif
 #endif
 
 #include "arch.h"
@@ -50,6 +41,14 @@ john_register_one(&fmt_sapG);
 #include "johnswap.h"
 #include "memdbg.h"
 
+#ifndef OMP_SCALE
+#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
+#define OMP_SCALE               32
+#else
+#define OMP_SCALE               2048
+#endif
+#endif
+
 #define FORMAT_LABEL            "sapg"
 #define FORMAT_NAME             "SAP CODVN F/G (PASSCODE)"
 #define ALGORITHM_NAME          "SHA1 " SHA1_ALGORITHM_NAME
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `src/sapG_fmt_plug.c`**
   - Removed the previous definition of `OMP_SCALE` that was set to 128 for the case when `SIMD_COEF_32` is defined.
   - Introduced a new definition of `OMP_SCALE` set to 32 when `SIMD_COEF_32` is defined, and retained the definition of 2048 for the else case.
   - The new definition of `OMP_SCALE` is now placed after the inclusion of necessary headers, ensuring it is defined correctly based on the conditions.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `src/sapG_fmt_plug.c` address a bug related to the incorrect testing of `SIMD_COEF_32` before its definition. By redefining `OMP_SCALE` to a lower value (32 instead of 128) when `SIMD_COEF_32` is defined, the patch aims to optimize the performance of the SAP-G format, particularly in the context of OpenMP scaling. This change also aligns the scaling factor more closely with the multiplier used for length sorting, which is intended to improve the overall functionality and efficiency of the code. The patch effectively resolves the issue introduced in a previous commit (27c9bf17) and closes the related bug report (#3050).

 SIMD_COEF_32 was tested before defined. Also down-tunes OMP_SCALE so it
 resembles the multiplier used for length sorting. Closes #3050.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect definition and testing of `OMP_SCALE` before the `SIMD_COEF_32` was defined, leading to an inappropriate scaling factor being used for OpenMP, which affected the performance and functionality of the SAP-G format.

-#ifndef OMP_SCALE
-#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
-// Some OMP scaling moved into max_keys, so that we can have more values in SIMD

-#define OMP_SCALE               128
-#else
-#define OMP_SCALE               2048
-#endif
-#endif

```c

```
Reason:
The bug occurs because `OMP_SCALE` is defined based on the condition of `SIMD_COEF_32` being defined, but this check is performed before `SIMD_COEF_32` is actually defined. This results in an inappropriate scaling factor being used for OpenMP, which negatively impacts the performance and functionality of the SAP-G format.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#ifndef OMP_SCALE
#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
#define OMP_SCALE               32
```
Reason:
The fix involves redefining `OMP_SCALE` after ensuring that `SIMD_COEF_32` is properly defined. This change adjusts the scaling factor to a more appropriate value (32 instead of 128), which aligns better with the intended performance characteristics for the SAP-G format, thus resolving the issue.
